chunks: He said: And I heard Abul Hasan Ali ibn Bilal ibn Muawiyah al-Mahlabi say regarding the lifetime of Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Quluwayh that he heard Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Quluwayh al-Qummi say: I heard Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Matil al-Qummi say:

Muhammad ibn Uthman, Abu Ja'far al-Amari (may Allah be pleased with him), had about ten people in Baghdad who managed affairs for him, and Abul Qasim ibn Ruh (may Allah be pleased with him) was among them. All of them were closer to him than Abul Qasim ibn Ruh, so much so that when he needed a matter or a task to be fulfilled through someone else's hand, because Ibn Ruh did not have that specific proximity, when the time came for the passing of Abu Ja'far (may Allah be pleased with him), the choice fell upon him and the will was entrusted to him.

key_terms.ابن روح: Ibn Ruh, a prominent deputy of the Imams
key_terms.الخصوصية: Proximity/special closeness, referring to the level of intimate access to the Imam
key_terms.العمري: Al-Amari, referring to Muhammad ibn Uthman
key_terms.الوصية: The will/authority, referring to the final designation or trust

ai.seo_question: Who was chosen as the successor to Muhammad ibn Uthman among the Imams' deputies?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* clarifies the succession dynamics within the four prominent deputies (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'a) during the Minor Occultation, distinguishing between daily administrative proximity and ultimate spiritual authority. It highlights Abul Qasim ibn Ruh’s selection as the final executor of Imam al-Hadi’s will, underscoring the continuity of the Imamate’s hidden guidance through a structured chain of trusted representatives.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 336 - The narrator  says: I heard from Abul Hasan Ali bin Bilal bin Muawiyah Mahlabi that he said about the life of Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Quluwayh that he heard from Abul Qasim Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Quluwayh that he said on the authority of Ja’far Ibn Ahmad Ibn Matil Qummi

that Muhammad Ibn Uthman Abu Ja’far Amari had about ten people in Baghdad who were his deputies. Abul Qasim Ibn Ruh was one of them. All of them were closer to him than Abul Qasim Ibn Ruh so much so that when he needed something or had a task, he would have it fulfilled through someone else, because Ibn Ruh did not have that kind of proximity to him. When Abu Ja’far was to pass away, the choice was his and he had the authority to make his final will.
